n: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Nazaré
w: The Sanctuary of Our Lady of Nazare was founded in the 14th century on the clifftop known as O Sitio, above the fishing town, to mark a Marian miracle attributed to the Virgin's intercession. It remains a major pilgrimage shrine, its hilltop position giving commanding views down over Nazare and the Atlantic.
_facts: Located on the O Sitio clifftop above Nazare

w: First built in 1577 and remodelled repeatedly since, the Fort of Sao Miguel Arcanjo guards the coast at Nazare and now serves as both a working lighthouse and a museum. Its fame rests largely on its ringside view of the giant-wave surf break just offshore, drawing visitors as much for the waves as the walls.
s: 1577 fort turned lighthouse and surf museum
_facts: Functions as both lighthouse and museum
Overlooks Nazare's famous big-wave surf break

w: Discovered in 1961 by Eduino Borges Garcia, the Igreja de Sao Giao in Famalicao parish is reckoned one of the oldest temples on the Iberian Peninsula. Long assumed Visigothic and 7th-century, later scholarship pushed it to the 10th century instead, pointing to Asturian origins. It holds National Monument status.
s: Iberia's oldest temple, misdated for decades
_facts: Discovered in 1961 by Eduino Borges Garcia

w: The Memory Hermitage, or Chapel of Our Lady of Nazare, sits at the very edge of the Sitio promontory above town. Four-sided and topped with a pyramidal roof, its walls are covered in blue-and-white tiles, marking the exact spot where tradition holds the Marian miracle took place.
s: Tile-covered chapel marking the Marian miracle's spot
_facts: Also called Chapel of Our Lady of Nazare
Sits on the edge of the Sitio promontory
Four-sided, pyramidal roof, blue-and-white tiled walls
